claims.text: This dispute is safety-flagged and the record bears it out: the driver wrote 'U think I free ah? Come down now or I come up find you' (MSG-05068-003), and the rider answered 'Why are you talking to me like that? I'm scared to come down now' (MSG-05068-004). Under POL-GEN-21 a dispute whose record carries a threat or a rider feeling unsafe is escalated to human review whatever the category the filer chose, and the AI may not issue a ruling, determine fault or recommend a resolution on it. The category label 'NO_SHOW_CHARGE' cannot take this case out of POL-GEN-21; the safety indicator is on the face of the chat log, and the chat log is complete, contiguous and carries weight 1.0.

The driver's answer, 'I was joking only. Passenger very late.', does not withdraw the words; a threat to come up and find a rider is still a threat on its face, and POL-GEN-21 names 'a threat', 'verbal harassment' and 'a rider or driver feeling unsafe' as safety indicators that force human review. The rider's fear is contemporaneous and in the log, sent at 22:21:00 before the 22:22:50 cancellation, and it was read by the driver at 22:21:33 — the driver cancelled eleven seconds' worth of record later with the rider's fear in hand. Whether it was a joke is exactly the fault question POL-GEN-21 reserves to the human reviewer.

POL-NS-26 makes an AI ruling on a no-show final only 'subject to POL-GEN-21 (safety)'. That carve-out is the whole of this case: because the safety flag fires, the AI's finality does not attach and the 5.00 SGD fee cannot be fixed by the AI. The fee that was charged at 22:22:54 must go to a human reviewer, not be ratified here.

Escalation is not a neutral outcome for the rider: under POL-GEN-03, ESCALATE is always terminal, replaces any ruling, and no monetary outcome issues — the amount is held. The ledger shows 5.00 SGD charged at 22:22:54 with refund_issued_sgd 0.00, so this is the disposition that stops the disputed charge from being collected and transferred to the driver while the threat the rider reported is reviewed by a human.

There is no countervailing referral available against this rider: POL-NS-25's repeat-no-show flag applies only where rider_profile.no_show_cancellations_30d is present, and the rider snapshot carries no such field, so the flag cannot fire whether or not the fee stands. That removes the only profile-based referral the policy permits on the rider's side of a no-show, leaving the safety escalation as the disposition the record supports.

Nothing about the GPS trace displaces the escalation. The trace corroborates only that the driver sat at the pickup from 22:16:20 to 22:22:50 — it says nothing about the message the driver sent at 22:20:30, and POL-GEN-21 does not require the safety incident to be a driving incident. Where the arrival facts are settled but the safety question is not, the case still goes to the human reviewer; POL-GEN-26 confirms that the AI does not bridge a gap by inference.

claims.text: The driver reached the pickup: the trip record's arrival event at 22:16:30 is corroborated by the GPS trace, whose nearest qualifying fix (index 13, at 22:17:20, reported accuracy 4 m) lies about 1.0 m from the pickup point — far inside the 50 m arrival radius for a STANDARD pickup zone — so the arrival test under POL-NS-21 is satisfied.

The free wait ran from the driver's arrival at 22:16:30 (this was an on-demand trip, scheduled_at is null, so under POL-NS-21 the wait runs from arrival, not a schedule) and expired at 22:21:30; the rider was still not on board — she had written 'Coming, 2 min' at 22:19:10 but the wait timer expired with the rider not on board — and the driver cancelled 80 s later at 22:22:50. POL-NS-21 therefore permits the cancellation and POL-NS-22 authorises the 5.00 SGD no-show fee.

The driver's contact obligation under POL-NS-23 is fully met: the chat log shows two driver in-app messages before cancellation (MSG-05068-001 at 22:16:50 and MSG-05068-003 at 22:20:30) and the trip record shows one in-app call placed by the driver at 22:18:00 (rang 15 s), all before trip_record.cancelled_at 22:22:50. Both limbs — message and call — are present, so the fee cannot be voided on POL-NS-23 and the rider is not entitled to a FULL_REFUND on that ground.

The amount charged is exactly the policy fee: the payments ledger records a single 5.00 SGD cancellation-fee line (total_charged 5.00, payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00), identical to the 5.00 SGD no-show fee in POL-NS-22. The fee charged therefore equals the fee the driver is owed as compensation for time and fuel, and no fee-amount referral under POL-NS-22 arises.

POL-NS-24 has no application here: its trigger is a driver who fails to reach the pickup within five minutes of the applicable time, whereas the record shows the driver arrived at 22:16:30 (GPS-corroborated) and waited 380 s, so the rider's no-charge cancellation right never arose and no 5.00 SGD goodwill credit is due.

POL-GEN-26 does not turn this case into an evidential escalation: the specific facts it makes escalation-worthy are all established on this record — when the driver arrived (22:16:30, corroborated by the GPS trace) and whether the driver messaged and called before cancelling (both, per the chat log and the in-app call record) — so there is no open question of the kind POL-GEN-26 addresses.

This dispute is flagged safety-related (dispute.safety_flag is true) and the record carries a safety indicator — the driver's message MSG-05068-003 and the rider's reply that she was scared to come down — so POL-GEN-21 routes it to human review whatever category the filer chose. Under POL-GEN-03 an ESCALATE issues no monetary outcome and holds the amount, so the properly-charged 5.00 SGD fee is held rather than refunded: no FULL_REFUND can be ordered on this record, which preserves the driver's position pending review.
